summary: Dependency-confusion beacon exfiltrates host identifiers to hardcoded bare IP at install and require time
details: The package is a stub with no real functionality (described as a 'compatibility shim') under the scoped name @webapp-shared/ with implausibly high version 99.0.1 — the shape of a dependency-confusion squat. On install, package.json runs `node beacon.cjs` as a postinstall script, and the main entrypoint index.js calls `require('./beacon.cjs').fire()` on load, so the beacon fires both at `npm install` and on any require. beacon.cjs POSTs a JSON payload containing the package name, `os.hostname()`, `__dirname` install path, `process.cwd()`, and `process.version` to the hardcoded bare-IP cleartext HTTP endpoint http://13.140.137.222:8787/_ah/dc. index.js exports a Proxy no-op so consumer builds complete without errors, concealing that the module provides no functionality. The transmitted host identifiers disclose internal hostnames and filesystem paths of installers whose private-registry resolution was captured by the scoped squat, enabling targeted follow-on supply-chain attacks against those environments.
